name: ai_gateway.tenant_credential.* event contracts
skipReason: Contract-only change in packages/contracts/src/events.ts. The three event types ai_gateway.tenant_credential.{bound,rotated,revoked}.v1 are emitted by the bind/rotate/revoke endpoints (TK-3448/3449/3450). Producer-side correctness is exercised by those endpoints' integration tests; this file is only an anchor for the contracts task.
description: Contract-only anchor for the three ai_gateway.tenant_credential.{bound,rotated,revoked}.v1 event types declared in packages/contracts/src/events.ts, all registered with regulated retention and an event-sourcing conflict policy. They are emitted as a side effect of the bind (POST), rotate (PATCH) and revoke (DELETE) /api/ai-gateway/tenant-credentials endpoints. QA edge cases: this definition declares no runtime surface — there is no route, no handler and therefore no error response of its own, so producer-side correctness must be asserted through those three endpoints' integration tests rather than here; the security-critical property to verify on the producer side is that no event payload ever carries raw_key or credential_envelope (last_4 and binding metadata only); because retention is 'regulated' these events are subject to the longer retention class, and because emission is best-effort inside the credential service a successful 2xx from bind/rotate/revoke does not by itself prove the event was appended.

testCases.name: Three event types registered with regulated retention

_fieldEnumsSource: packages/contracts/src/events.ts:8-9 — `export type RetentionClass` and `export type ConflictPolicy`. All three ai_gateway.tenant_credential.* entries (events.ts:506-508) pick retention_class='regulated' and conflict_policy='event-sourcing': a credential binding change is a compliance record, and event-sourcing is the only policy under which the bound -> rotated -> revoked sequence stays readable as a history rather than being collapsed to a last-writer-wins snapshot.

errorCases.message: [ai-gateway.byok] audit emit failed for bind|rotate|revoke <binding_id> <reason> (console.error only)
errorCases.when: appendAuditEntry() throws inside tenantCredentialService bind (line ~228), rotate (~298) or revoke (~368). Each emit sits in its own try/catch that only console.errors, so the bind/rotate/revoke endpoint STILL returns its 2xx while the regulated-class event is lost. A green producer test therefore proves nothing about the event — QA must read audit.entry for the binding_id.

the name is absent from EVENT_TYPE_REGISTRY in packages/contracts/src/events.ts (lines 506-508 register all three) — assertRegisteredEventType throws and OC-2 rejects the append before any write. Because the emit is swallowed, a rename or a dropped registry line degrades to exactly the case above: a clean 2xx with no ledger row.

errorCases.message: event_type '<name>' does not follow the naming convention <domain>.<entity>.<verb>.v<N>
errorCases.when: validateEventTypeName() (contracts/src/events.ts:625-633) refuses a name missing the mandatory .v<N> suffix or using uppercase. Reachable when a consuming application registers a look-alike type through POST /api/events/types; the three platform names here already satisfy the pattern, and the .v<N> suffix is what lets the payload shape change as a new version instead of silently redefining rows already written.

errorCases.message: (no error is raised — this one fails silently and is the reason to assert it)
errorCases.when: a payload field is added carrying raw_key or credential_envelope. Nothing rejects it: the payload is jsonb and the three emits name their fields explicitly (binding_id, tenant_id, provider_id, last_4, actor_id, timestamps, model_allowlist, fallback_on_error). Because retention_class is 'regulated' the leaked secret would then be kept for the LONGEST retention class, in an append-only chain that cannot be edited to remove it.

_noRuntimeSurfaceNote: This file declares no route and no handler, so it has no HTTP status of its own; every case above is what the PRODUCER endpoints (POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/ai-gateway/tenant-credentials) do or fail to do when emitting. Listing them here rather than leaving errorCases empty is deliberate: the failure modes of a best-effort emit are invisible in the producer's own response, which is exactly why they need writing down.
